areas.m: Trackers: Committee of 100 (2023 report Table 1; July 2026 map page), Make Us Visible state chapters, K-12 Dive, Northwest Asian Weekly. Primary: act/statute/bill text on legislature sites (IL, NJ, RI, FL, NE, NV, WI, CA, CO, OR, UT, ME, DE, WA, MD, MA, AK, AZ, HI, NY) and agency pages (ISBE, CSDE). Search quota ran out before per-state checks of 2025-26 bills in remaining states; 'none' means not found in these trackers.
notes: Search quota ran out mid-run. 2025-26 bill status was directly checked only for AK, AZ, MD, MA, NY, WA, ME, DE. Other 'none' states rest on trackers (C100 2023 and July 2026, Make Us Visible, K-12 Dive); C100 says 7 states have pending bills as of July 23, 2026 but its state list is in a Shiny map I could not read, so some pending bills may be missed.

Tracker disagreement on counts: C100 (July 2026) says 13 states have Asian American studies statutes; its 2023 report named 11 (CA, CO, CT, FL, IL, NE, NV, NJ, OR, RI, UT). Make Us Visible counts 8 mandate states (IL, NJ, CT, RI, FL, WI, DE, ME) and omits CA, CO, NE, NV, OR, UT. This table: 11 enacted, 15 partial, 1 pending, 24 none.

Classification calls: CA, CO, NE, NV, OR are enacted because the statute names Asian American and/or Pacific Islander history inside a required curriculum or standards, though as part of multi-group lists. UT is partial (ethnic studies mandate; AAPI named only in a definition). DE and ME are partial (see cells); MUV counts both as mandates.

Standards-only states (AL, AZ, IN, MN, MS, TN, VA, DC from C100 2023 data; OK and IA from C100 July 2026) are marked partial because C100 calls the standards required curriculum. I did not open any state standards document, and the 2023 list may be stale. C100 says 17 states have such standards in 2026; I can name 15 states plus DC (AL, AZ, CA, CT, FL, HI, IN, MA, MN, MS, OK, OR, TN, VA, IA); the other 2 are unidentified.

Hawaii: no statute found; the Hawaiian education program mandate is in Haw. Const. art. X sec. 4 and covers Native Hawaiian language, culture and history only. Marked partial under the lower-status rule. Hawaii statute pages were blocked (Cloudflare) so implementing statutes could not be searched.

Primary text not reached: Connecticut statute text (cga.ct.gov TLS error; relied on CSDE page and news), Illinois statute page (ilga.gov TLS error; Public Act and ISBE page read through the fetch tool), Wisconsin statute (read via the fetch tool, not directly). Several quotes (IL, CT, WI, NY) come from page text as relayed by the fetch tool.

Dead or stalled bills noted as none: AK SB 6 (Senate-passed 2025, House Finance 2026), AZ SB 1301 (held in House 2025; AZ is partial for standards), MD HB 1323 (2025) and HB 1059 (2026), WA SB 5574 (died Feb 2026). Adjournment dates were not confirmed on a fetched page. Massachusetts H.604 is the only bill I confirmed as still sitting in committee.

New Jersey: chapter is numbered P.L. 2021 c. 416 but approval date is 1/18/2022; y is set to 2022 (C100 says 2021). Delaware regulation update under SB 297 and Maine's July 2029 effective date are not verified beyond the session-law text.
Utah 2026 HB 399 (would have restructured 53E-4-204.1) has no enrolled version at le.utah.gov, so it appears not to have passed; Utah's ethnic studies section was last amended in 2025.

notes: Coverage limit: the web search budget ran out before a fresh sweep of 2025-26 bills in most states. none cells rest on the Leadership Conference Education Fund trackers (research current to Sept 2023; report updated Oct 2024; 2025 page lists 13 states) plus spot checks. Laws enacted after mid-2025 may be missing.

Hawaii: the Oct 2023 Zellers review counts HB1983/SB811 as a law requiring subgroup categories, but enacted Act 136 (2023) only created a task force. The Oct 2024 update of Disaggregation Nation removed Hawaii from its list. Rated partial.

No pending cells: no bill alive in the 2025-26 cycle was confirmed for a non-enacted state. Texas SB 2390/HB 3564 sat in committee after 3/25/2025. Washington SB 5784 was in Senate Ways & Means on 11/2/2026, but Washington is already enacted.

California: AB 2132 was named in the task but not found in any source read. The subgroup statutes trace to AB 1088 (2011, Gov. Code 8310.5 and 8310.7) and AB 1726 (2016, adds CDPH). The Leadership Conference calls 8310.7 a '2022 law'; CDPH cites AB 1726 with a July 1, 2022 start date.

New York: year entered as 2021 (signed Dec 2021, amended by a 2022 chapter amendment). The Leadership Conference cites 'Chapter 18' of the Laws of New York; I did not verify the chapter number. A separate MENA law (Exec. Law 170-h) is not an Asian/NHPI measure.
Minnesota: Zellers describes the law as applying to 'certain school districts'; current Minn. Stat. 120B.35 subd. 3 text applies to the commissioner's reporting categories generally.

Connecticut: the statute (PA 21-35 Sec. 11) defers to OHS subgroup standards. The OHS web page now carries a notice that agency functions were realigned under PA 26-68 effective 6/30/2026; I did not verify what happened to the standards.

Vermont is unclear: 18 V.S.A. 253 requires race/ethnicity health data disaggregated beyond White/non-White, per a recommendation I could not find. Illinois, Nevada and New York 170-h add MENA categories, which are not counted as Asian/NHPI disaggregation.

New York quote was copied from the NewYork.Public.Law mirror when first read; the mirror returned HTTP 503 on a later automated re-check, so the quote could not be re-matched. The 2021 bill text (A6896A) is the primary source.

Not reachable from this environment: wearethedata.us (D-DAN interactive map), leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, nysenate.gov and ilga.gov via curl. Mirrors (California.Public.Law, NewYork.Public.Law, OregonLaws) were used for current code text and are marked non-primary.

Washington's 2026 law (SHB 2475, Ch. 142) is rated partial because it sets policy, guidelines (due 12/1/2027) and agency reports (6/30/2028) rather than a direct service mandate, and states it creates no new rights. Reviewers may prefer enacted.

MPI counts MA (EO 615), NC (Governor's Office policy) and DE as cross-agency. Here MA and NC are partial (executive action, no statute found) and DE is unclear. Pennsylvania (EO 2024-01 plus a 2025 program) is not on MPI's list; its EO text was not retrieved, only a state press release.

Pending bills: no state without a law was confirmed to have a live bill. MA H.3384 and S.2622 sit in Ways and Means (last action Oct 2025) but MA is already partial. Year conventions: Hawaii 2006 (MPI, NCIHC) although the chapter was recodified as 321C by L 2012 c 201; Maryland 2002 per NCIHC and the 2002 bill (MPI says 2003); NJ 2024 is the signing year (P.L. 2023, c.263); Michigan 2023 acts took effect Feb. 28, 2024.

Access problems: capitol.hawaii.gov, nysenate.gov, mass.gov and California's leginfo blocked automated fetches; text came from data.capitol.hawaii.gov, NewYork.Public.Law plus the NY OGS page, a press release, and CalHR plus a university mirror of the statute. ilga.gov failed TLS checks in curl, so Illinois Act text was read through the fetch tool; the quote comes from the Governor's ONA page.

WI read via FindLaw mirror; CA, CO, NY, TX via Public.Law mirrors; IL via ilga.gov through a fetch tool; CT text is the 2021 DCJ compilation.

Connecticut P.A. 26-77 (SB 90, signed 5/26/2026) revised and consolidated the hate-crime statutes; the new text was not reviewed, and status stays enacted based on the prior statute and the Act's title.

Arkansas and Indiana are partial: Ark. Code 5-4-405 (Act 681 of 2021) and IC 35-38-1-7.1(a)(12) (2019) address victim-group or bias selection without naming race, ethnicity or national origin. MAP and Brennan do not count either as a hate-crime law; ADL and others may differ.

North Dakota (civil-rights-style offense limited to use of public facilities) and Ohio (ethnic intimidation limited to menacing, property-damage and harassment offenses) are partial under the 'choose the lower status' rule; some trackers count both as having hate-crime laws.
Enacted entries that are sentencing factors or enhancements rather than stand-alone offenses include AK, AZ, KS, KY, MS, NM, TN, TX, ME and WI; Alaska's list says 'creed' rather than 'religion'.

South Carolina: H.3039/S.247 (Pinckney Hate Crimes Act) were not enacted; a May 13, 2026 report said the session ended May 14 with the bill expected to stall. Marked none rather than pending because no evidence shows the bill alive after adjournment; final action not independently confirmed.
Wyoming: no hate-crime statute per MAP and WACH (May 2026); a title search of all 2025 and 2026 bills in the Legislature's data found no hate or bias bill, so none rather than pending.

The web-search budget ran out before sweeps for 2025-26 bills that would amend existing statutes; amending bills are mentioned only where seen (North Carolina H961, 2025). Mississippi bills to expand categories (e.g., HB 364 of 2024, died in committee) were not tracked for 2026.
Data-collection remarks in x come from MAP's citations document and describe whether a state mandates collection; they do not state whether reports go to the FBI except for New Mexico.

Statutes or bills read on legislature sites for AZ FL ID IA KS LA MA MN MO NC NE NY OH OK SC SD TN TX UT VA WV; other states from NALC statute text. Court status from 5th/11th Cir. opinions and CourtListener RECAP dockets.
notes: Scoring rule used: 'enacted' = broad real-property coverage that reaches individuals or private persons by nationality/domicile, or non-citizens generally (FL, IN, NE, OK, TN, TX, WV). Laws limited to farmland, to military/critical-infrastructure proximity (AL, GA, KS, MT, NC, AR), or to governments/state-controlled entities (AZ, LA, ND, UT, SD) were scored 'partial' under the brief's lower-status rule; a reviewer who reads 'critical-infrastructure-adjacent' as 'enacted' can re-map those.

Source conflicts: Committee of 100 reads AZ SB 1683 and TN SB 2424 as government-only, but the AZ chaptered text adds 'foreign person' (31 CFR 802.221) to 'agent' and TN's bill text covers citizens/residents of ITAR countries. C100 and NALC list different country sets for Indiana SEA 256. NALC's July 2026 slides describe AZ SB 1082's threshold as '30% of real property'; the statute sets an interest threshold (30%, cut to 15% by SB 1683).

Web search was unavailable after mid-session, and the NH, MI, PA, OH, NJ and CA legislature sites could not be queried. 'Pending' was verified only for NY (A09031); MA H.141 and SC S.1065 were checked and are effectively dead. Other 'none' cells mean no enacted law found, with live 2025-26 bills unverified. Committee of 100 reported 7 states with 23 bills pending on 8/13/2026 without naming them.

Unconfirmed enactments: SD SB 60 (2026; enrolled text has no signature date; Leonine lists SD as enacted), OK HB 3431/SB 893 (enrolled copies lack signatures; NALC/C100 say enacted), MS SB 2341, LA SB 466/HB 192, IA/NE 2026 measures, and the NH measure (cell is 'unclear'; Leonine names NH without a bill number).

Court status: Wang v. Paxton (5th Cir. 25-20354) affirmed dismissal for lack of standing on 12/11/2025 (court opinion; RECAP shows terminated that day). Shen v. Simpson: 11th Cir. opinion 11/4/2025; RECAP shows the district case terminated 12/31/2025 and ACLU-FL says voluntarily dismissed. Jones Eagle (8th Cir. 25-1047, argued 1/14/2026) and Huang (5th Cir. 25-51034, briefs filed) rest on RECAP docket text and may lag. Secondary summaries disagree on these cases.

NALC compilations are dated by legislative session (CO through 2021; CA, CT, DE, HI through 2024; most others through 2025) and mostly cover farmland; non-farm laws (e.g., KS SB 9, NC HB 133) were found through other sources, so other non-farm military-proximity laws could be missing.

Hawaii, Oregon, Maryland, New Jersey and Maine were scored 'none' as judgment calls: each has only a public-land, conditional-permission or non-foreign-specific reporting rule. Alaska and DC are outside NALC's compilation and were not searched in their own codes.

Texas AG rulemaking (proposed Chapter 67 rules, 3/27/2026) was seen only in a secondary tracker and not verified. Statute text for IN, ND (via NALC), OK, WI, PA, IL, KY, MS, MT, GA, AL, AR, ID is from NALC compilations or trackers unless a primary source is listed in the cell.
